verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents a first-party MCP server, including a hosted version, that lets users manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language from MCP-capable AI clients such as Cursor and Claude Code. The natural-language interface depends on an external AI client rather than an in-product assistant, and the documented scope covers flags, configs, and observability rather than the whole product. missing for 10: an in-product natural-language interface, documented natural-language coverage beyond flags/AgentControl/observability (e.g., experiments, members, approvals), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: To get started with the LaunchDarkly MCP server, you enable the server, then use it to manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language.
Configure the hosted MCP server so you can manage feature flags and AgentControl configs, and view observability data, directly from your AI client.
you must have an AI client that supports MCP, such as Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code with Copilot, or Windsurf.
